title: Universal integral factorization of a quasi-compact separated algebraic-space morphism
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], and work with algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space] in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention], with sheaf fibre products [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers] and atlas point topology [def-a1-space-point-topology]. A morphism $g:A\to C$ is quasi-compact if for every quasi-compact scheme $T$ and every morphism $T\to C$ the sheaf fibre product $A\times_CT$ admits a representable surjective etale map from a quasi-compact scheme [def-weil-etale-morphism]. Separated means that the relative diagonal is representable by closed immersions [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Integral means representable by integral morphisms of schemes on every scheme test [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. Let $f:Y\to X$ be quasi-compact and separated. There exist an algebraic space $N$ and morphisms $i:Y\to N$ and $n:N\to X$ with $ni=f$, such that $n$ is integral and the following universal property holds: for every algebraic space $T$, integral morphism $q:T\to X$ and morphism $a:Y\to T$ with $qa=f$, there is a unique morphism $h:N\to T$ satisfying $hi=a$ and $qh=n$.

source.place: Tags 0822 (definition-normalization-X-in-Y) and 0823 (lemma-characterize-normalization); the separated specialization of the quasi-compact quasi-separated relative normalization.

proof.text: First record the formal mapping correspondence needed below. For any $g:Z\to X$ and any quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-algebra $\mathcal D$, maps $Z\to\operatorname{Spec}_X\mathcal D$ over $X$ are sections of $Z\times_X\operatorname{Spec}_X\mathcal D\to Z$, by the fibre-product universal property. Base change in the relative-Spec correspondence identifies this with $\operatorname{Spec}_Z(g^*\mathcal D)\to Z$. Its sections correspond contravariantly to $\mathcal O_Z$-algebra maps $g^*\mathcal D\to\mathcal O_Z$: the identity of $Z$ corresponds to $\mathcal O_Z$, and composition with the structure morphism is the unit equation. Tensor pullback/direct-image adjunction identifies these maps with $\mathcal O_X$-algebra maps $\mathcal D\to g_*\mathcal O_Z$. Explicitly the transpose sends $b\otimes d$ to $b\chi(d)$; this preserves products and units precisely when $\chi$ does. The inverse is restriction of functions along the given map. These inverse correspondences respect composition: precomposing an algebra map composes the resulting space maps in the reverse order. This is just the cited anti-equivalence, base-change identity and adjunction, not an assumption that $g$ is affine.

source.place: Tag 081V (lemma-affine-equivalence-algebras), base change and contravariance; Remark 081X (remark-factorization-quasi-compact-quasi-separated), counit construction, written as a mapping correspondence.

proof.text: Put $\mathcal A=f_*\mathcal O_Y$ with multiplication and unit induced by regular functions. The module $\mathcal O_Y$ is quasi-coherent, being free on one generator; the quasi-compact separated pushforward theorem therefore makes $\mathcal A$ quasi-coherent. Its hypotheses hold: quasi-compactness of $f$ on all quasi-compact scheme tests includes the affine tests in that theorem, and separatedness is the same closed-relative-diagonal condition. Apply the integral-closure lemma to obtain a quasi-coherent subalgebra $j:\mathcal B\hookrightarrow\mathcal A$. Set $N=\operatorname{Spec}_X\mathcal B$ and let $n:N\to X$ be its structure map. On every affine etale chart $U\to X$, every element of $\mathcal B(U)$ is integral over $\mathcal O_X(U)$. The integral-algebra criterion of the relative-Spec correspondence gives that $n$ is representable and integral on scheme tests, exactly as required. The inclusion $j$ corresponds by step 1 to a map $i:Y\to N$ over $X$, so $ni=f$.

source.place: Tag 03M9 (lemma-pushforward), Tag 0820 (lemma-integral-closure), Definition 0822 (definition-normalization-X-in-Y), and Tag 081V with the integral test of Tag 03ZQ (lemma-integral-local).

proof.text: Take any $q:T\to X$ integral and $a:Y\to T$ with $qa=f$. An integral morphism is affine on scheme tests by the definition of an integral scheme morphism. The relative-Spec correspondence consequently writes $T=\operatorname{Spec}_X\mathcal C$, where $\mathcal C=q_*\mathcal O_T$ is quasi-coherent and $\mathcal C(U)$ is integral over $\mathcal O_X(U)$ on every affine etale chart $U\to X$. Step 1 associates to $a$ an $\mathcal O_X$-algebra map $\chi:\mathcal C\to\mathcal A$. If $c\in\mathcal C(U)$ obeys $c^r+\sum_{k<r}d_kc^k=0$, applying $\chi_U$ gives $\chi_U(c)^r+\sum_{k<r}d_k\chi_U(c)^k=0$. Hence $\chi_U(c)\in\mathcal B(U)$. These factorizations commute with restrictions because both maps become $\chi$ after inclusion in $\mathcal A$; affine etale charts cover the site, so they define a unique algebra map $\bar\chi:\mathcal C\to\mathcal B$ with $j\bar\chi=\chi$. Contravariance gives $h:N\to T$ over $X$, thus $qh=n$. The composite $hi$ corresponds to $j\bar\chi=\chi$, so the bijection in step 1 gives $hi=a$.

source.place: Tag 0823 (lemma-characterize-normalization), proof of (2), including the monic-polynomial check and verification of the two triangles omitted there.

proof.text: If $h':N\to T$ also satisfies $qh'=n$ and $h'i=a$, its algebra map over $X$ is $\psi:\mathcal C\to\mathcal B$. Composition in the relative-Spec correspondence and step 1 turn $h'i=a$ into $j\psi=\chi=j\bar\chi$. Since $j$ is the inclusion of a subalgebra sheaf, componentwise injectivity gives $\psi=\bar\chi$. Faithfulness of the anti-equivalence gives $h'=h$. This proves uniqueness among all space morphisms satisfying the two equations, without any finiteness or representability hypothesis on $a$.

proof_origin.place: Tags 0822 and 0823, constructed using Tags 03M9, 0820, 081V; mapping correspondence and commutative triangles expanded.
